messages:
violet: quick heads-up: small spike in nvme read error counts and a few badblock remap events on ephemeral drives in eu-west3 starting 04:12 UTC. GPUs failed attach briefly, autoscaler reported pending pods. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/storage/drive-errors?var-region=eu-west3 :warning:

mike: saw that, 5 hosts with remap_count > 3. attach_waits jumped but overall IOPS didn't change much. looks like intermittent retries causing tail latency.

dara: dug into node logs, janitor was running a concurrent scrub across the rack and hit the same partitions that are heavily used by GPU snapshots. sample log from ip-10-20-33-7:

```
Mar 20 04:12:07 janitor[1123]: remap detected on nvme0n1p1, remap_count=4
Mar 20 04:12:08 kernel: nvme0n1: I/O 0x7ff... timeout, retry
Mar 20 04:12:09 janitor[1123]: scrub: backoff 150ms due to read retry
```

jihoon: quick actions: 1) reduced janitor concurrency on the 5 hosts to 1, 2) set `redwood.io/avoid-gpu-attach=true` annotation to keep allocator from scheduling new GPU pods there for 10m, 3) applied node cordon on two worst hosts. commands used: `kubectl annotate node ip-10-20-33-7 redwood.io/avoid-gpu-attach=true --overwrite` and `sudo sed -i 's/concurrency: 4/concurrency: 1/' /etc/janitor/config.yaml && sudo systemctl restart janitor`

violet: after those changes attach_waits recovered in ~6 mins. p95 attach latency dropped from ~240ms -> 45ms. good quick win.

mike: hardware note: the affected drives are a mix of older FlashEdge-600 and newer FlashEdge-900. remap patterns cluster on the older ones; recommend flagging them for vendor health check and possible replacement.

dara: follow-ups: 1) implement a soft-throttle in janitor if remap_count > 2 or if kernel retry rate > threshold, 2) add allocator preference to avoid nodes with recent remaps for 30m, 3) add Optimize suggestion to stagger scrub windows from snapshot-heavy workloads.

ops-bot: [alert] attach_wait.eu-west3 resolved (5 hosts). Incident window 04:12-04:18 UTC.

jihoon: I'll open a hardware ticket and schedule a probe to run an offline scrub on a single canary drive this weekend. also adding a console toggle to let teams pick "safe scrub" during heavy snapshot activity.

mike: and let's add a metric `nvme.remap_recent` to the host exporter so allocator rules can use it.

violet: thanks all. filing retro note and tagging infra-ops for replacement list. :memo:
